prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show an open parking area with the camera wearer roughly 2–5 m from a table, chairs, loudspeakers, canopy, and several people; the ground immediately below the camera is nearest, while trees, lamps, and parked vehicles are farther away, mostly about 6–20+ m. A person on the left is about 2–3 m away in frame 1, a person near center-left is about 2–3 m away in frame 2, and more distant people remain roughly 4–10 m ahead in later frames; the nearest people and equipment appear mutually separated by about 1–3 m. Across the sequence, the camera view turns right, moving the left-side person out of view and bringing a central loudspeaker and then the right-side people and car into prominence; apparent depth changes mainly reflect this rotation rather than clear approach or retreat. The depth map makes near–far ordering and ground distance gradients clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable on the bright sky, thin poles, foliage, object edges, and the loudspeakers, whose very bright values may exaggerate their nearness; none of the mapped objects is clearly within the camera wearer’s arm reach.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks identify multiple people, several cars, and a chair clustered around the canopy and equipment, with people generally in front of or beside the cars and the chair low between nearby equipment; their RGB-scale distances are approximately 2–4 m for the closest people and chair, 4–8 m for the cars and other people, and greater for the background. In frames 1–2, a large person mask stands left or center-left and another person is near the table, while car and chair masks overlap spatially behind or beside them; in frames 3–5, the view shifts right and smaller people and car masks occupy the center and right, with a close person entering the lower-right area in frame 5. The masks expose partial occlusions that RGB makes difficult to separate, especially people overlapping cars, tables, speakers, and one another, and they show several bodies truncated or fragmented by those objects or by the frame boundaries. Facing direction and gaze are mostly indeterminate from the masks, though some side-on body silhouettes suggest people facing across the scene rather than squarely toward the camera; the map is unreliable because masks are fragmented, several visible objects such as speakers and tables are unlabeled, labels overlap, and some people or object parts are missed.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides one usable body skeleton only in the second frame, corresponding to the nearby person about 2–3 m ahead and left of center; the head is above the torso, the legs extend downward, and one raised arm reaches toward the head while the other lies nearer the torso. This skeleton clarifies limb placement that is less distinct in RGB and suggests the body is oriented partly sideways or obliquely rather than directly square to the camera, but head orientation is too coarse to establish whether the person is looking at the camera wearer. The hands and body are not shown close enough to the camera to be within the wearer’s arm reach, while the raised hand is within that person’s own arm reach of the head; nearby equipment appears roughly 1–2 m from that person, although the pose map does not encode objects or metric depth. No reliable skeletons appear in frames 1 or 3–5 despite visible people, so the map cannot support their positions, occlusions, facing directions, or motion and is highly incomplete for changes across the sequence.
